FINDINGS (both non-blocking; neither is this PR's to fix):
F1. The body calls the lwb-proof-reexecute digest mismatch "one pre-existing, structural, out-of-scope mismatch in a different already-merged PR's own record". Measured: lwb_check_proof.py --reexecute is EXIT 0 on unmodified main ("ALL RE-EXECUTED COMMANDS MATCHED", 24/146 across 21 records) and EXIT 1 on this branch (proof/39.json, lwb_handoff.py --check digest). So it is NOT pre-existing: this PR causes it, because HANDOFF.md goes 2961 -> 2958 bytes and proof/39.json recorded a digest of output containing that byte count. The same sentence of the body does disclose exactly that mechanism, so this is an inaccurate label rather than a concealed failure. NOT BLOCKING: .github/workflows/ci.yml:130-164 runs that step with continue-on-error: true and documents at length why it is report-only, so it cannot fail the job. The real residue is structural and general: any PR that changes HANDOFF.md's byte length invalidates proof/39.json's recorded digest. Worth a follow-up (record a byte-count-insensitive command, or exempt it), not a change to this PR.
F2. VACUOUS GUARD, pre-existing on main: a proof record's 'commit' field is only shape-checked. lwb_check_proof.py:152-154 tests it against COMMIT_RE (hex, 7-40 chars) and nothing else; it is never checked for reachability on the branch or for naming the commit it purports to name. Proved by P4 above. Consequence: D2 -- one of the two findings this PR exists to fix -- is protected by no mechanical check and can silently regress. Coverage matching does not catch it either: check_pr_has_record/_landed_deliverables prefer the typed 'pr' field, so a wrong 'commit' is never surfaced there. This PR neither introduced this nor claims it is guarded; recorded here for a follow-up that validates 'commit' resolves to a commit reachable from the PR head.

NEAR-MISSES I MADE AND CAUGHT (recorded because hiding them makes this record worth less):
- N1. My first pass compared each open PR's existing records against the RAW branch head and concluded all five open PRs were unreviewed at their head. That is wrong. _review_ok compares reviewed_commit against resolve_reviewable_head, which skips record-only commits; a record can never name the raw head, because committing it moves the head. Re-measured: #45 (reviewable head 073034f), #44 (108d87d), #43 (a31f0ef) and #40 (4793afc) each already carry a record naming their exact reviewable head. Only #46 was genuinely unreviewed. Uncaught, I would have filed four duplicate reviews on heads that already carry verdicts.
- N2. I nearly charged lwb_handoff.py --check with being vacuous about the proof-record count, having watched it pass with a falsified "21/21 proven". It is indeed silent on the count -- _validate only checks the size cap, required headings, marker pairing, forbidden paths and needles -- but the count is caught precisely by lwb_check_state_claims.py (P1). I had aimed the probe at the wrong guard. The ordering trap IS mechanically guarded; reporting otherwise would have been a false accusation against a correct document.
- N3. Twice my own harness produced "I could not check" wearing the face of "I checked and found nothing" -- the exact defect class this repository hunts. (a) My first test run was `python -m pytest tests/ -q 2>&1 | tail`, which printed "No module named pytest" while the pipeline returned exit 0; pytest was not installed for this interpreter and I briefly recorded the suite as passing. Installed pytest 9.1.1 and re-ran for the real 522. (b) `lwb_lanes.py` without --base exits 2 on argparse, but my `echo exit=$?` after a pipe read tail's 0. Both re-run capturing the script's own status. Every number in this record comes from a run whose real exit code I captured.
